24: Fort Collins climbs two spots since mid-March to reach No. 1, and it gets there with the best collection of arms in the league. R.J. Blum, the top prospect in the game, anchors the system as a starter whose stuff and stamina both project as elite, with plus movement and control, a plus fastball and elite splitter and sinker; he is at Triple-A, and his 4.93 ERA over 38 1/3 innings hasn't yet matched the ceiling. Leo Gatica (No. 26) brings a plus fastball, slider and circle change at Double-A, Brian Holder (No. 32) has already reached the big leagues out of the bullpen, and David Santiago (No. 79) has a 1.96 ERA at A+. With seven Top 100 prospects, elite grades in both blue-chip talent and depth, and the fifth-best readiness mark, the Roosters offer the most complete package around.
12: Oahu slips one spot from its mid-March perch at No. 1, but the Paddlers still own an elite blue-chip and depth profile, led by 19-year-old center fielder Carlos Navarro (No. 5), whose hit tool, gap power and speed all project as elite, with a plus glove and plus plate discipline; the only real question is over-the-fence power, which grades below average. Casey Emerson (No. 16), the No. 1 overall pick in the 2031 Draft, has a plus slider, changeup, cutter and sinker at A+, and Gary Walters (No. 40) pairs elite stuff with an elite fastball and cutter, though his control lags. Shortstop Ron Clark (No. 52) is hitting .325/.390/.437 at Triple-A with a plus glove. Six Top 100 names and 11 overall in the top 200 make this one of the deepest groups in the league.
5: Vancouver moves up two spots to No. 3 on the strength of a loaded group of bats. Jeremy Austin (No. 6), the fifth overall pick in the 2031 Draft, projects as elite in power, gap power and plate discipline with plus speed, and he is joined in Rookie ball and A- by Luis Ramirez (No. 27) and Micah Patterson (No. 93), two more outfielders with elite gap power. Kevin Stover (No. 66) is hitting .303/.392/.462 at Double-A with a plus hit tool. The arms are thinner and shakier: Jarrod Bensel (No. 14) has elite stamina and a plus changeup and sinker but a 6.07 ERA at Double-A, and Ernie Flores (No. 128) carries a fragile durability grade. Elite blue-chip talent and plus depth carry the ranking, but the lopsided balance keeps the Vandals from climbing higher.
20: Somerville holds steady at No. 4, buoyed by elite depth and the second-best readiness score in the league. This is a bat-first system, with six of its seven top-200 prospects on the hitting side. Kevin Miller (No. 38) has plus power, plus hit and plate discipline and elite gap power at A+, Terrell Moody (No. 56) projects as an elite hitter, and 21-year-old Willie Schultz (No. 154) is tearing up A with a .427/.509/.729 line and six homers in 96 at-bats. Eric Aasen (No. 70) is a plus defensive catcher a step from the majors at Triple-A. Sebastian Croslin (No. 84), the lone arm, has elite stuff, stamina, fastball and curve, but his control grades well below average. Six Top 100 prospects give the Moneyline a strong, ready-made foundation.
6: Toronto jumps four spots to No. 5, powered by the league's third-best pitching group. The headliner is 19-year-old Ron Turner (No. 10), the tenth overall pick in the 2031 Draft, who has plus stuff, movement and stamina, an elite fastball and a plus slider, and is holding a 3.38 ERA at A. Turner is joined by control specialists Brent Michalski (No. 43) and Jose Alonso (No. 102), each with elite control. On the hitting side, Mike Larson (No. 11) projects as an elite hitter with elite gap power at Triple-A, though his over-the-fence power and discipline grade below average, and first baseman Alex Moralez (No. 64), who has elite power, is already in the majors and has 13 homers in 174 at-bats. Blue-chip talent is elite, with a plus balance across hitters and pitchers.
26: Huron gains five spots to No. 6 with 12 prospects in the top 200, tied for the most in the league, and several of them have already reached the majors. Outfielders Kyle Stevens (No. 23) and Yuji Kishi (No. 24) are both in the big leagues, Stevens with elite gap power and speed and Kishi with an elite hit tool. Kyle Edwards (No. 47) has elite stamina and plus control there as well, and reliever Ethan Clark (No. 124) pairs elite stuff with an elite fastball and curve. Matt Ray (No. 101) is hitting .291/.386/.558 at A+, and Andy Hurst (No. 111) has a .402/.469/.537 line at Double-A. The system leans heavily toward hitters, but plus blue-chip talent and plus depth make it one of the steadiest in the league.
1: Myrtle Beach falls five spots to No. 7, and the reason is easy to see: this is the league's best hitting system and one of its most one-sided. Shortstop Bill Sanchez (No. 8) has plus power, plus discipline, plus speed and a plus glove with elite gap power, hitting .283/.327/.558 at Triple-A, while Andy Hummer (No. 30) has a .295/.368/.598 line there. Ben Sloan (No. 19), the 18-year-old selected 11th overall in the 2031 Draft, projects as an elite hitter with elite gap power and discipline and a durable grade. Chris Acevedo (No. 107) has 13 homers and a .349/.408/.658 line at Double-A. The pitching, however, is the weak link, ranking 19th in the system rankings, and the balance grade well below average holds the Mermen back despite elite depth.
18: San Juan climbs five spots to No. 8, helped by a pair of 2031 draftees. Adam Rall (No. 17), the sixth overall pick, has plus hit and power, elite gap power and plus discipline, and is hitting .274/.335/.473 at Triple-A. Reliever Matt Giglio (No. 62), a second-rounder, brings an elite fastball and elite stuff, though his control needs work. Frank Mildner (No. 37) has 13 homers and a .259/.360/.601 line in the big leagues, and catcher Chris Cobble (No. 113), a 20-year-old, is hitting .378/.410/.622 at A. Clint Dukeshire (No. 22), a center fielder with plus hit, elite gap power and a plus glove, adds more at Double-A. The bats rank fourth in the system rankings, while pitching depth remains an area to build.
8: Baltimore drops two spots to No. 9, but its farm stands out for how close to the majors it is: the Blue Crabs rank first in readiness. Three prospects, including Danny Cox (No. 29), who is hitting .303/.341/.529 at Triple-A, and catcher Alex Mojica (No. 67), have a 2032 arrival on the table. Rick D'Amore (No. 25) is the best of the younger group, with plus power, elite gap power and elite plate discipline and a .344/.453/.625 line at A+. Dave Dougherty (No. 51) and David Manley (No. 83) add plus hit tools and elite gap power in the outfield, and Antonio Razo (No. 122), an outfielder with elite gap power and speed, is already in the big leagues. Ten top-200 prospects and plus depth back the case, though the pitching side ranks 13th.
9: New Orleans slides two spots to No. 10, though it still boasts seven Top 100 prospects and 12 in the top 200. Alejandro Vargas (No. 13) is the headliner, a Triple-A infielder with plus hit and power, elite gap power and speed and plus discipline, although he is hitting .220/.337/.312 so far. Dave McCloy (No. 58) offers elite gap power and plus speed at Triple-A, and Felipe Rodriquez (No. 77) has a plus hit tool. On the mound, Jugurtha Kimya (No. 75) has plus stuff and control with a plus fastball, cutter and sinker, striking out 13.5 batters per nine innings in the big leagues, though his ERA sits at 5.06. Plus blue-chip talent and eight hitters in the top 200 provide the foundation.
13: Las Vegas moves up three spots to No. 11, thanks to a system ranked third in readiness. Shortstop Manuel Salas (No. 48), with plus power, gap power, speed and a plus glove, and infielder Frank Williams (No. 73), who is hitting .324/.347/.559 with a plus hit tool, are both already in the majors, with Salas' .188/.249/.333 line the one concern. Beyond them, the bullpen arms stand out: Cameron Stetler (No. 98) and Eric Archie (No. 148) both have elite stuff and an elite fastball, with Stetler adding an elite slider, though both have stamina that grades well below average. Ken Grossman (No. 117) has plus control and stamina and a 3.73 ERA at A, and the pitching ranks eighth overall. Plus depth is the real strength here.
21: Memphis rises three spots to No. 12 on the strength of a strong top end and an exciting young pitching group, even with the system still far from ready to help. Mike Jenkins (No. 4) is the crown jewel, an infielder with an elite hit tool, elite gap power and plus discipline who is hitting .300/.380/.500 at Double-A; power is the one area that lags. Efrain Rosales (No. 31), the third overall pick in the 2031 Draft, has plus stuff, movement and stamina with an elite cutter and a plus changeup at Rookie ball. Chris Faulk (No. 42) is hitting .323/.429/.516 at A+ with elite speed and plus hit and discipline, and 16-year-old Carlos Rios (No. 168) has elite gap power and a plus glove. Plus blue-chip talent carries the ranking, but readiness ranks 31st.
19: Southland falls three spots to No. 13, and the split between hitting and pitching is stark: the bats rank second in the system rankings while the pitching ranks 26th, with just one arm in the top 200. Christian Lombera (No. 12) has plus hit, elite power and plus gap power and discipline at Triple-A, and Steve Boettcher (No. 87), a 21-year-old, is hitting .391/.478/.713 with seven homers at Double-A, backed by an elite eye. Zack Maurer (No. 72) is another 21-year-old first baseman with elite gap power and discipline and plus power and speed, and Alvin Phillips (No. 21) adds elite gap power and a plus glove in the outfield. Six Top 100 prospects and plus depth keep the Masked Bandits in the top half, but the balance grade is well below average.
3: Philadelphia falls two spots to No. 14, a top-heavy system that owes much of its standing to one player. J.P. Schall (No. 3), the 12th overall pick in the 2031 Draft, has elite power and gap power, plus discipline, plus speed and a plus glove in center, and is hitting .301/.378/.521 at Triple-A with a 2032 arrival possible. Behind him, the group thins out quickly: Ian Cathey (No. 57) has elite stuff and an elite slider but stamina that grades well below average, Edwin Martinez (No. 65) has plus control and stamina, and Andy Taran (No. 114), a 20-year-old, has plus movement and a plus fastball at A+. Four Top 100 prospects give the Eagles a reasonable blue-chip grade, but depth grades below average.
15: Oklahoma City gains a spot to No. 15, with a farm that is defined by pitching and near-term readiness. The Outlaws rank fourth in readiness and 10th in pitching, led by Dustin Hayes (No. 80), a 25-year-old with plus movement and stamina who owns a 2.82 ERA over 44 2/3 innings at Triple-A. Felix Rosario (No. 118) is even sharper at Double-A, where his 2.17 ERA over 49 2/3 innings comes with elite stamina, plus movement and a plus slider and changeup, and Josh Seibel (No. 104), an elite-stamina starter, is in the big leagues. The 2031 draft class adds outfielders Eddie Cochran (No. 130) and Jeremy Hoffmann (No. 188), who is hitting .342/.383/.461 at A+. Just one Top 100 prospect leaves the blue-chip grade average, but a plus balance is a strength.
22: Boston nudges up one spot to No. 16 despite having just four prospects in the top 200, thanks to two very good arms. Josh Owens (No. 2) is one of the best pitching prospects in the game, with plus stuff, movement and control, elite stamina, a plus fastball and elite curve and splitter; he owns a 2.47 ERA over 51 innings at Triple-A. Jimmy Gant (No. 44), the second overall pick in the 2031 Draft, has elite stuff and an elite curve, though his control grades below average. Blake Elmore (No. 99), a catcher, could arrive this year. The bats are the issue, ranking 26th in the system rankings, and the depth grade is below average, and an elite balance grade reflects the even split between bats and arms.
23: Big Horn takes the largest tumble of any system, dropping 11 spots to No. 17, the result of a thin system now defined by one player. Ernesto Sanchez (No. 7), a first baseman with plus hit and power, elite gap power and plus speed, is hitting .297/.338/.469 at Triple-A and could arrive in 2032. Beyond that, the top 200 offers just two more names: center fielder Geoff Danser (No. 135), a 20-year-old with elite gap power and a plus glove, and Jim Marge (No. 189), the 26th overall pick in the 2031 Draft, who has plus control and a plus fastball, curve and changeup at A-. Blue-chip talent grades below average, but plus balance and average depth keep the Rams in the middle of the pack.
215: Kansas City holds at No. 18 with a farm built around the 2031 Draft. Three of its five top-200 prospects came from that class: Casey Ady (No. 145), a catcher with a plus glove, reliever Jason Seifert (No. 150), who has plus stuff and movement with a plus fastball and slider, and Chris Turner (No. 184), a 19-year-old starter with plus stuff and movement, taken 24th overall. Pedro Huante (No. 91), an outfielder with plus power and seven homers at Double-A, is the lone Top 100 prospect, and Josh Herrington (No. 147) offers plus movement and control. The pitching ranks 11th while the hitting ranks 25th, and an elite balance grade is a positive, but blue-chip talent grades below average.
11: Denver rises two spots to No. 19 on the strength of its youngest hitters. Gustavo Perez (No. 46), a 20-year-old outfielder, projects as elite in power, gap power and discipline with plus speed, and 17-year-old Odilon Keating (No. 82), still at the international complex, has elite power and discipline. Catcher Dylan McCreedy (No. 178) is hitting .303/.365/.500 at A with a plus glove, and reliever Sake Oostvogels (No. 185) brings an elite fastball and plus curve at Double-A. Chris Enriquez (No. 129) and Alex Suazo (No. 172), both starters at A, add depth to the pitching. Seven prospects in the top 200 and an average blue-chip and depth grade put Denver in the middle of the pack, though the readiness rank of 28th says most of it is years away.
16: Tampa Bay climbs three spots to No. 20, led by three Top 100 prospects. Jeff Raymond (No. 68), a 19-year-old infielder and the fourth overall pick in the 2031 Draft, projects as elite in power and gap power with plus discipline and speed at A-. Robby Clem (No. 36) has plus hit, power, gap power and discipline at Triple-A, while Ryan Affrunti (No. 39), a 21-year-old starter, has elite stamina, plus movement and control and is holding a 3.67 ERA at Double-A. Chris McMillian (No. 119) has elite power, with 12 homers and a .268/.337/.524 line in the majors. There are only four top-200 prospects, and the readiness rank of 32nd, dead last, means none of it is close to helping soon.
4: Spokane rises one spot to No. 21 with three Top 100 prospects and a system that grades as average across the board. Jonathan Montano (No. 28), the eighth overall pick in the 2031 Draft, is the best of the bunch, a Triple-A starter with plus movement, elite stamina and a plus fastball, slider and sinker who has a 4.87 ERA over 44 1/3 innings. Manny Alers (No. 60), a designated hitter with plus hit, discipline and speed, is in the big leagues, and David Guerrero (No. 162), a 21-year-old, has elite power. Dustin Mast (No. 85) has plus gap power and speed at Triple-A. Just one pitcher in the top 200 keeps the pitching ranking at 24th.
25: Montreal slips two spots to No. 22, a system that is heavily tilted toward outfielders. Chris Shere (No. 50), the lone arm in the top 200, has plus stuff, control and stamina with an elite sinker at Double-A, though his 7.64 ERA over 35 1/3 innings has not helped. Jonathan Anthony (No. 92), a 20-year-old outfielder with elite power and discipline and a durable grade, and 19-year-old Paul Hesselbrock (No. 197), the 22nd overall pick in the 2031 Draft, who has elite power, gap power and discipline, provide the ceiling. Edwin Garcia (No. 110) is hitting .397/.473/.615 at A+, and Andrew Abrams (No. 155) has a .375/.420/.594 line at A. Seven top-200 names make this a reasonably deep group, though blue-chip talent grades below average.
10: Milwaukee drops four spots to No. 23, a system built on speed and hitting depth rather than star power. Manuel Ruiz (No. 35), an infielder with plus hit, gap power and speed, is at Double-A, while outfielders Bryan Sarro (No. 74) and Frank Kerr (No. 200) both grade as elite runners, with Sarro adding elite gap power at Triple-A. Larry Leppert Jr. (No. 55), the only pitcher in the top 200, has plus movement, control and stamina with a plus fastball and changeup at Double-A, though he has a 4.79 ERA over 41 1/3 innings. Four Top 100 prospects and average depth keep the Mobsters from falling further, but a balance grade below average reflects the lack of pitching, and none of the six top-200 names came from the 2031 Draft.
17: Cincinnati climbs four spots to No. 24, and one prospect explains much of it. Bobby Avila (No. 9), a 16-year-old outfielder, projects as elite in power and discipline with plus gap power and speed, though he is years away at Rookie ball. Beyond him, catcher Mauricio Dominguez (No. 53) is a plus defender at Triple-A who could arrive this year, Josh Boucher (No. 142) has elite power, plus speed and a plus glove in center field and a durable grade, and reliever Chris Talford (No. 171) pairs plus stuff with an elite cutter. The bats rank 11th but the pitching ranks 29th, with just one arm in the top 200, and depth grades below average and balance well below average.
27: San Diego holds at No. 25 with a small but interesting group. Jessie Hughes (No. 54), a 21-year-old starter, has plus stuff, movement and control, elite stamina and an elite fastball with a plus slider, and he is dominating Double-A with a 1.53 ERA over 53 innings, though his durability grades as fragile. Tyler Joyner (No. 61), a catcher with plus power, is hitting .321/.391/.564 at Triple-A and could arrive in 2032, and Willie Perez (No. 105) offers a plus hit tool, elite gap power and plus speed. Only three prospects make the top 200 and blue-chip talent and depth both grade below average, but a plus balance grade shows the talent is not lopsided.
216: Mexico City drops two spots to No. 26, and this system is entirely made up of hitters, with the bats ranking 15th and the pitching 30th. Kevin Clarke (No. 15), a 21-year-old outfielder with plus hit, power and gap power, is hitting .214/.287/.297 at Double-A, a slow start for the system's best prospect. Ian McIlree (No. 20), a catcher with a plus glove, could arrive this year, hitting .244/.331/.420 at Double-A, and Bobby Kraemer (No. 166) adds another catching option at A+. With just three top-200 prospects and both depth and balance grading well below average, the farm has little margin for error.
28: Phoenix slips one spot to No. 27, with a system built on athletic hitters and one exciting arm. Willie Villalba (No. 49), a 20-year-old starter, has plus stuff and movement with a plus fastball, cutter and sinker at A-. Victor Calderon (No. 109), the 27th overall pick in the 2031 Draft, has plus power, elite gap power and discipline and plus speed at Double-A, while shortstop Casey Morris (No. 127) offers a plus glove and plus speed at Triple-A. Jay Seabolt (No. 137), a designated hitter, is hitting .295/.345/.500 with seven homers at Triple-A and could arrive in 2032. One Top 100 prospect and below-average grades across blue-chip talent, depth and balance keep the Firebirds near the bottom.
14: Galveston moves up one spot to No. 28, though the top of the system is sparse: Kyle Saale (No. 158), a 24-year-old outfielder with a plus hit tool but below-average discipline, is the only prospect in the top 200 and is hitting .213/.291/.347 at A+. The organization has no one in the Top 100 and its blue-chip talent grades well below average. Still, the system ranks sixth in readiness and carries a plus balance grade, with average depth.
2: Chicago drops two spots to No. 29 with a system defined by young pitching. Roberto Garcia (No. 34), an 18-year-old starter at the international complex, has plus stuff and movement with an elite fastball and curve and a plus changeup, and is the lone Top 100 prospect. Ben Nicholson (No. 120), a 21-year-old at Double-A, has plus control and a plus fastball and a 3.35 ERA over 40 1/3 innings, and infielder Ernesto Olaya (No. 190) offers a plus glove. The bats rank 31st in the system rankings and depth grades well below average, but an elite balance grade shows how evenly, if thinly, the talent is spread.
7: Virginia holds at No. 30 with a farm that has almost nothing at the top. Dave Shahan (No. 196), a 20-year-old outfielder with plus power and gap power, is the only prospect in the top 200, hitting .269/.367/.436 with three homers at A+. The pitching ranks dead last in the system rankings, the bats rank 28th and blue-chip talent grades well below average, though the balance is average. The Rebels have work to do at every level to rebuild the pipeline.
213: Rochester holds at No. 31 with a farm that has one player in the top 200. Chris King (No. 132), a 20-year-old starter at A+, has elite movement and control but below-average stuff, and his durability grades as fragile. The hitting ranks last in the system rankings, blue-chip talent and depth both grade well below average, and the elite balance grade reflects how little there is to balance. Development at the lower levels will decide whether the North Stars can rebuild.
214: New York holds at No. 32, with a thin system where one prospect, Joe Weiner (No. 106), is the only name in the top 200. The 23-year-old center fielder has plus speed and a plus glove but below-average discipline, and he is hitting .245/.280/.447 with five homers at Triple-A. The bats rank 30th and the pitching 31st in the system rankings, and both blue-chip talent and depth grade well below average, so the Empire's rebuild will have to start at the lower levels.
